planning_scheme.notes: Council page states "Livingstone Planning Scheme 2018 (Version 4)" and that the scheme commenced 1 May 2018; all v4 part files are stamped "V4_Adopted_2025_02_18". Appendix 2 Table A2.2, amendment 3 (Version 4, minor amendment - zone map changes): adopted 18 February 2025, published in the Government Gazette 2 May 2025, "in effect: 2 May 2025". Gazette No. 2 (Local Government) of 2 May 2025: "The commencement date for the amendment is 2 May 2025." v4 only changed zone/precinct mapping; text provisions (incl. Schedule 10) unchanged since Version 3 (package 3 amendments, gazetted 5 February 2021). QHC: no reference to the Queensland Housing Code was found in Part 1, Part 5, the zone codes or Schedule 1; the scheme has not adopted the QHC (council-specific Schedule 10 setbacks apply as alternative provisions).

qdc_qhc_relationship.summary: Part 1 s1.6 states the scheme, through Part 5, regulates building work under ss32 and 33 of the Building Act 1975, and lists relevant zone codes and the Seaspray Local Plan as building assessment provisions. Table 5.6.1 makes standalone Class 10a building work accepted subject to requirements against zone-code setback AOs, which adopt the Schedule 10 setback tables (SC10.1.1-SC10.1.4, SC10.1.9-SC10.1.10). These operate as alternative boundary-clearance provisions to QDC MP1.1/MP1.2 for Class 10 in the zones covered. No QHC adoption found.

definitions.text: Setback, for a building or structure, means the shortest distance, measured horizontally, between the outermost projection of the building or structure to the vertical projection of the boundary of the lot where the building or structure is.
A non-habitable class 10a building that is: (a) a shed, garage or carport; and (b) ancillary to a residential use carried out on the premises where the building is.
Means a Class 10a building, other than a garage, providing covered vehicular parking.

Means a carport with: (a) two sides or more open, and a side is also considered open where the roof covering adjacent to that side is not less than 500 millimetres from another building or a side or rear lot boundary; and (b) not less than one-third of its perimeter open.

Outermost projection, of a building or structure, means the outermost part of the building or structure, other than a part that is: (a) a retractable blind; or (b) a fixed screen; or (c) a rainwater fitting; or (d) an ornamental attachment.

Outermost projection height, for a building or structure, means the vertical distance between any point of the building or structure at its outermost projection, and the ground level directly below that point.

Mean height, of a building or structure, means the vertical height worked out by dividing the total elevational area of the wall of a building or structure facing the boundary by the horizontal length of the building or structure facing the boundary.
Means either: (a) the dimension at right angles to the road boundary; or (b) the average of the relevant dimensions at right angles to an irregular road boundary.
The boundary of the lot aligned with the road from which the street address is allocated.

A residential use of premises involving: (a) one (1) dwelling for a single household and any domestic outbuildings associated with the dwelling; or (b) one (1) dwelling for a single household, a secondary dwelling and any domestic outbuildings associated with either dwelling.

rules.verbatim_text: AO5.1 Buildings or structures (other than fences) have a setback from road frontage lot boundaries in accordance with the following: (a) where located on a lot which has an approved building location envelope, the development is within the boundaries of the approved building location envelope; or (b) where located in the Seaspray Residential Low Density Precinct or the Seaspray Residential Medium Density Precinct and the lot does not have an approved building location envelope: (i) a setback from the primary road frontage lot boundary of at least six (6) metres; and (ii) a setback from a secondary road frontage lot boundary of at least three (3) metres; or (c) where located in the Seaspray Community and Recreation Precinct and the lot does not have an approved building location envelope: (i) a setback from any road frontage lot boundary of at least six (6) metres.

rules.notes: Seaspray local plan code prevails over zone codes (s1.5(d)). Table 5.8.1.5 makes standalone Class 10a building work in all Seaspray precincts accepted subject to requirements against AO5.1 and AO5.2 (among others). Where the lot has an approved building location envelope (BLE), the BLE governs instead (plans held by Council). Fences are excluded. Underlying zone of the Seaspray area not confirmed; scoped by local plan precinct. Dwelling houses are not identified as accepted/code in this precinct (Table 5.8.1 MCU tables list dwelling house for the residential precincts); included for completeness.

rules.alternative_provision_to_qdc_qhc: YES - Part 1 s1.6(3): "This planning scheme, through Part 5, regulates building work in accordance with sections 32 and 33 of the Building Act 1975." and s1.6(4)(c) lists "Relevant zone codes" (and (e) "Seaspray Local Plan") as building assessment provisions; the s1.6 editor's note cites "alternative boundary clearances and site cover provisions for Class 1 and 10 structures under section 33". Table 5.6.1 makes standalone Class 10a building work accepted subject to requirements against these AOs.
rules.measurement_notes: SC1.2 Setback: "the shortest distance, measured horizontally, between the outermost projection of the building or structure to the vertical projection of the boundary of the lot where the building or structure is." Outermost projection excludes a retractable blind, fixed screen, rainwater fitting or ornamental attachment. Outermost projection height is measured to ground level directly below that point.

rules.verbatim_text: AO5.2 Buildings or structures (other than fences) have a setback from side and rear lot boundaries in accordance with the following: (a) where located on a lot which has an approved building location envelope, the development is within the boundaries of the approved building location envelope; or (b) where located in the Seaspray Residential Low Density Precinct or the Seaspray Residential Medium Density Precinct and the lot does not have an approved building location envelope: (i) a setback of at least 1.5 metres; or (c) where located in the Seaspray Community and Recreation Precinct and the lot does not have an approved building location envelope: (i) at any point where the ‘outermost projection height’ is between two (2) metres and 4.5 metres, a setback of at least ten (10) metres; or (ii) at any point where the ‘outermost projection height’ is greater than 4.5 metres, a setback of at least ten (10) metres plus 0.3 of a metre for every additional metre or part thereof in height over 4.5 metres.

local_plan_mechanism.summary: One local plan: Seaspray Local Plan (precincts LPP-01 Seaspray Residential Low Density, LPP-02 Seaspray Residential Medium Density, LPP-03 Seaspray Community and Recreation). Local plan codes prevail over zone codes (s1.5(d)). Building work in the local plan area is categorised by Table 5.8.1.5 against Seaspray local plan code AO5.1/AO5.2 (6 m primary frontage; 1.5 m side/rear in the residential precincts; or an approved building location envelope). Zone precincts with setback variations: Rural zone Yaamba Historic Township Precinct (AO10.1, 20 m). Rural residential Park Residential Precinct uses the <1 ha row of Table SC10.1.4. Emerging community: Schedule 10 applies only outside local plan / approved structure plan areas.

open_questions: Underlying zone(s) of the Seaspray Local Plan area were not confirmed (mapping not checked); Seaspray rules are scoped by local plan precinct only. Confirm whether the zone-code Schedule 10 setbacks also apply there (Table 5.6.1 vs Table 5.8.1.5).
Emerging Community Zone: Schedule 10 does not apply in approved structure plan areas / preliminary approvals (which may set their own setbacks or building envelopes); these are not captured.

Swimming pools are not named in Schedule 10; whether an in-ground pool is a 'building or structure' with an outermost projection height over 2 m (and so subject to the 6 m front setback) needs curator interpretation.
Raw scope "Rural Zone" (ZONE level) also covers the Yaamba Historic Township Precinct, where AO10.1 applies instead of Schedule 10; consumer must give the precinct rule precedence.
Medium density / Major tourism Table SC10.1.3 second row (outermost projection height > 10 m) not recorded as separate rules.
Figures SC10.1.5-SC10.1.8 (corner truncation, secondary frontage, open carport, rural example) are images only and were not transcribed.
